us.label: US News
us.subtitle: Top domestic headlines from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: Federal judge extends order blocking White House reporter ban
bullets: A federal judge extended an order Tuesday blocking the administration’s reporter ban.
The case involves three news outlets covering the White House.
The dispute continues as a major press-access legal fight.

articles.title: Republicans retreat from some front-line House districts
bullets: AP reported shifting battle lines in House races ahead of midterms.
Republicans are pulling back from some front-line districts.
The moves reflect changing campaign calculations late in the cycle.

articles.title: Trump heads to Alaska for GOP campaign push
bullets: Trump traveled to Alaska to campaign for Republican candidates.
The trip is part of a pre-midterms campaign blitz.
AP reported the visit on Tuesday, October 13.

articles.title: US recalls top envoy to Nicaragua after ambassador rejection
bullets: Secretary of State Marco Rubio recalled the top US envoy to Nicaragua.
Nicaragua rejected the administration’s ambassador nominee.
The envoy was recalled for consultations, AP reported.

articles.title: US existing home sales rise in September
bullets: Existing home sales rose 1.5% from August, CNBC TV18 reported.
Sales reached a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.99 million units.
August sales were revised lower, contributing to the monthly gain.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Russia still hitting Ukraine energy sites
bullets: Zelenskyy accused Russia of continuing aerial strikes on energy infrastructure.
The attacks came despite Trump’s ceasefire push.
AP reported the remarks from Kyiv on Wednesday.

articles.title: Trump says Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire agreed, Kyiv reports attacks
bullets: Trump said Russia and Ukraine agreed to an energy ceasefire.
Kyiv said Russian attacks on energy infrastructure continued.
Zelenskyy said Ukraine welcomed the announcement but faced drone attacks.

articles.title: Oil jumps after vessels struck in Strait of Hormuz
bullets: Oil rose after two vessels were struck in the Strait of Hormuz.
Reuters reported prices near $106 a barrel in the India market wrap.
Iranian officials said they were deploying new tactics targeting ships.

articles.title: Poland questions Musk over Starlink limits in Ukraine
bullets: Poland’s foreign minister asked Elon Musk if he was playing politics.
Kyiv said SpaceX limited some Starlink services.
Reuters reported the disruption affected Ukrainian combat drone missions.

articles.title: Russia arrests Japanese journalist on spying allegations
bullets: Russia’s FSB said it arrested a Japanese journalist on Sakhalin.
Authorities alleged he collected information on Russian defenses.
The Guardian listed the case among October 14 world headlines.

articles.title: India hosts first BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ meeting
bullets: India hosted the first BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ meeting.
The Delhi Declaration was adopted at the meeting.
The Indian Express listed it among October 14 India stories.

articles.title: Modi speaks with Canadian PM Mark Carney before likely visit
bullets: Prime Minister Modi spoke with Mark Carney, The Indian Express reported.
They discussed trade, technology, defense and an economic pact.
The call came ahead of a likely Canada visit.

articles.title: India rejects China objection over Ladakh naming
bullets: Delhi said Ladakh is an integral and inalienable part of India.
The response followed China’s objection over place names.
The item appeared in October 14 Indian news roundups.

articles.title: UPI fee on transactions above ₹2,000 postponed
bullets: A planned 0.4% merchant discount rate was deferred.
The change concerned UPI transactions above ₹2,000.
The New Indian Express reported implementation will follow Diwali.

articles.title: Indian shares close lower as oil and outflows weigh
bullets: Sensex declined 0.34% to 72,781.89.
Reuters cited higher oil prices and foreign outflows.

articles.title: Bank of America slips premarket after $1.21 billion fine disclosure
bullets: Bank of America shares fell 1.5% in premarket trading.
Reuters said the bank disclosed a $1.21 billion regulatory fine.
The charge could weigh on third-quarter results.

articles.title: Morgan Stanley edges higher before earnings
bullets: Morgan Stanley shares rose 0.7% premarket, Reuters reported.
The bank was set to report before Wednesday’s open.
Investors were watching another round of bank earnings.

articles.title: Johnson & Johnson drops despite profit beat
bullets: Johnson & Johnson fell 6.8% on Tuesday.
Reuters said healthcare was the biggest S&P 500 drag.
The decline came despite profit estimates being topped.

articles.title: Micron falls as chip stocks sell off
bullets: Micron Technology lost 4.6% in Tuesday trading.
Chip stocks faced pressure after China CXMT progress reports.
Broadcom CEO comments also hurt AI-stock sentiment.

articles.title: Apple hits record high during mixed tech trading
bullets: Apple reached a record high Tuesday, Reuters reported.
Microsoft also rose 0.9% during choppy trading.
Gains offset weakness in some semiconductor names.

articles.title: Wall Street awaits big bank earnings and CPI data
bullets: Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, BlackRock and State Street were due to report.
Investors also awaited key US inflation data.
Reuters said oil prices kept markets cautious.

articles.title: JPMorgan kicks off bank earnings wave
bullets: JPMorgan released third-quarter 2026 results on October 13.
The report came as earnings season moved into high gear.
MarketAlleys cited Yahoo and CNBC updates on the results.

articles.title: Goldman, Wells Fargo and Citigroup report amid earnings rush
bullets: Major Wall Street lenders reported results Tuesday.
Reuters described the bank earnings as a mixed bag.
Investors parsed financial-sector results before more reports Wednesday.

articles.title: ASML profit beats expectations as long-term order interest grows
bullets: ASML reported third-quarter net sales of €11.66 billion.
CNBC said profit beat expectations.
The company cited order interest reaching into 2029 and 2030.

articles.title: Bengaluru chemicals startup Scimplify raises $25 million
bullets: Scimplify raised $25 million led by Hitachi Ventures.
The startup uses AI agents to speed chemical production.
TechCrunch reported it works with 500-plus partner facilities.

articles.title: EU opens AI Act probes into OpenAI and Anthropic
bullets: The EU AI Office launched formal AI Act probes.
The probes concern AI agent hacks, Euronews reported.
Experts noted the law includes an R&D exemption.

articles.title: Nvidia pledges $250 million for UK AI safety research
bullets: Jensen Huang announced Nvidia’s five-year pledge.
The resources target AI security and agentic safety research.
Reuters reported the commitment on October 14.

articles.title: Rockstar’s GTA VI expected to generate billions after launch
bullets: Bloomberg reported on GTA VI’s development and expectations.
Analysts expect 40 million sales in four months.
Projected early revenue exceeds $3 billion.

articles.title: AI safety groups spend $48 million in midterm cycle
bullets: Axios analyzed AI safety spending in bipartisan races.
The money backs candidates favoring AI regulation.
Spending reached $48 million in the midterm cycle.

articles.title: Character.AI files for Chapter 11 with Disney as opening bidder
bullets: Character Technologies filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware.
Disney agreed to a $20 million stalking-horse bid.
Reuters said the chatbot platform aims to keep operating.
